title: Игнор от Елены и свадебный конверт  (Ignored by Elena and the Wedding Envelope)

segments.t: After dryly complimenting Max's speech and telling him to write it down later, Chef Barinov still refuses to take him back. Meanwhile, Viktor Petrovich grows increasingly frustrated when Elena declines his calls twice in a row just as Vika brings in the wedding clients.
Виктория, где вас черти носят, а?
Что мой будущий жених не смог прийти.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'Who do not value it very much.' Notice how Russian expresses 'who' and 'roads' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'That is why I do not want to leave this place.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'therefore' and finishing on 'to leave'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'That was a fine speech.' In Russian, the idea of 'dear' flows naturally into 'speech' without extra filler words.
'Write it down for me later.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'later' before landing on 'for me'.
Виктория, где вас черти носят, а?
'Viktoriya, where on earth have you been wandering, huh?' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'Viktoriya' and 'where' in a few short words. Vika answers right away.
'And what about yourself?' Vika anchors the line on 'and', while 'there is no' completes the thought.
'Saying she was not offended.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'offended' to negate the statement.
'Yet she hangs up on me for the second time.' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'to go' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Что мой будущий жених не смог прийти.
'That my future groom could not make it here today.' In Russian, the idea of 'what' flows naturally into 'to come' without extra filler words.
'That is quite alright.' Vika anchors the line on 'nothing', while 'terrible' completes the thought.
'An envelope. Oh.' In Russian, the idea of 'the envelope' flows naturally into 'about' without extra filler words. Vika answers right away.
'Right this way, please. Hello.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'beg' before landing on 'hello'.
'Why are you wandering around out there?' In Russian, the idea of 'what' flows naturally into 'somewhere' without extra filler words. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.
Виктория, где вас черти носят, а?
Что мой будущий жених не смог прийти.
